system.name: Notes
system.purpose: A small notes service: people write notes in a browser, and search finds them again.

sources.note: a worked example for the archlens guide, not a real repository

boundaries.label: Our infrastructure
boundaries.claim: Runs code we deploy; anything outside it we can only call, not change

components.name: Web app
components.responsibility: Lets a person write, edit and search notes.

components.name: API
components.responsibility: Authenticates the caller and is the only writer of note records.

components.name: Postgres
components.responsibility: Holds every note as the system of record.

components.name: Indexer
components.responsibility: Turns a saved note into a search document, out of the request path.

components.name: Search index
components.responsibility: Answers full-text queries over a copy of the notes.

components.name: Email provider
components.responsibility: Delivers the invitation email when a note is shared.

relations.what_crosses: A session cookie and the note body. Never a database credential.
Note rows, written in one transaction with the user id.
A note id and a version. Not the note body, so a slow index cannot slow a save.
The note body, read at the version the event named.
The searchable text and its note id.
A query string and the caller's user id, so results stay scoped to them.
A recipient address and a signed link. Never the note body.

facts.because: one writer means one place to enforce authorisation, and the worker can be restarted without fear
indexing happens after the save so a write never waits on it; a note can be missing from search for a second or two

facts.claim: An event carries an id, never a note body
facts.because: the queue is not a second copy of the data, so it can be drained or replayed without leaking anything

questions.title: What happens when a note is saved
questions.ask: Where does a note go when someone hits save?
questions.answer: The browser posts to the API, which writes the row and publishes an event. Indexing happens afterwards, so the save never waits on search.
questions.omits: Sharing and email, which no save touches.

questions.title: How search stays in step
questions.ask: If the index is a copy, how far behind can it be?
questions.answer: One event per save, consumed out of the request path. A note is searchable a moment after it is written, and the API scopes every query to the caller.
questions.omits: The browser, which never talks to the index directly.
